subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should declarative cron definitions be a core jobs.d/import-export feature, a plugin/ClawHub package backed by stronger cron APIs, or intentionally out of scope while SQLite remains the runtime store?
rationale: The user problem is real and current main does not solve it, but AGENTS.md and VISION.md push runtime state toward SQLite and optional capability toward plugin/API boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Design declarative source boundary first
options.body: Define whether the durable source is core jobs.d, import/export, or a plugin sync API before implementing the storage/config changes.

options.title: Keep SQLite-only runtime for now
options.body: Close or defer file-backed cron source work and document CLI/RPC/plugin workflows as the supported maintenance path.

options.title: Build core jobs.d directly
options.body: Accept the extra config/storage surface and require upgrade, symlink, delete/rename, state-preservation, doctor, and security proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Design declarative source boundary first
recommendation.body: Define whether the durable source is core jobs.d, import/export, or a plugin sync API before implementing the storage/config changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron SQLite persistence and docs history most directly routes the storage-boundary decision to steipete.
